phase-428 W5 (2026-09-06) — ledgering a recorded sweep finding. RANKED-18. This extension has a correctness defect that outlives the extension question, so it is recorded here and the upstream-facing disposition is on `cpp:Client::async_send_request`.

`send_request_sized` (`packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp/client.hpp:119`, the body both spellings share) constructs its future with a literal slot 0 (`:132`) and discards the sequence number. THREE layers drop the key: the FFI has no sequence out-param at all (`nros_cpp_service_client_send_request(storage, req_data, req_len)`, `packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp/detail/nros_cpp_ffi.h`); the Rust body discards it (`Ok(_seq) => NROS_CPP_RET_OK`, `packages/api/nros-cpp/src/service.rs:697`); `take_response` discards it again (`Ok(Some((len, _seq)))`, `:723`). And `Future::slot_` is not a key — it is only a consumed sentinel and is never passed to the take function.

HOW A USER FINDS OUT: SILENTLY WRONG. Two outstanding futures on one client both hold 0, both call the same `take_response` on the same storage, and whichever is polled first consumes whatever reply arrived. Nothing compile- or runtime-detects the cross-delivery. Re-verified by hand against the current worktree before this row was written.

The disposition for this finding is recorded on `cpp:Client::async_send_request`, which carries the full statement.
